column3: NASB renders “divorce” as “sends … away” and “letter of divorce” as “certificate of divorce.”
“Sexual immorality” is rendered “unchastity”; NASB supplies “woman” in “a divorced woman.”
“It was said to the ancients” becomes “the ancients were told”; “swear falsely” is “make false vows.”
Close to the Greek; “the city of the great King” is in capitals as a quotation.
“From the evil” is rendered “of evil”; the Greek may mean “of the evil one.”
NASB renders “strike” as “slaps” and supplies “person” after “evil.”
NASB follows the critical text; “bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you” and “mistreat you and” are from the Textus Receptus.
NASB follows the critical text with “Gentiles” and adds “than others.”
“You will be perfect” is rendered “you are to be perfect.”
